name: Supabase
description: Protects against destructive Supabase CLI operations including database \ resets, migration rollbacks, function/secret/storage deletion, project \ removal, and infrastructure changes

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-db-reset
destructive_patterns.description: supabase db reset drops and recreates the entire database. All data will be lost.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase db reset completely destroys and recreates your database:

\ - All tables, views, and functions are dropped \ - All data is permanently deleted \ - Migrations are re-applied from scratch \ - Seed data (if configured) is re-inserted

\ This is irreversible for any data not captured in migrations or seeds. \ With --linked, this targets the remote production database.

\ Before resetting: \ supabase db dump -f backup.sql

\ Review differences first: \ supabase db diff

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-db-push
destructive_patterns.description: supabase db push applies migrations to the remote database. Use --dry-run to preview first.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase db push applies pending migrations to the remote (linked) database:

\ - Migrations may include DROP/ALTER statements \ - Changes to the production database are irreversible \ - With --linked, this targets the live project database

\ Always preview changes first: \ supabase db push --dry-run

\ Dump remote database before pushing: \ supabase db dump -f backup.sql --linked

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-db-shell-destructive
destructive_patterns.description: supabase db shell with destructive SQL (DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE/ALTER). Verify the command carefully.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase db shell is being invoked with destructive SQL:

\ - DROP permanently removes database objects \ - TRUNCATE removes all rows from tables \ - DELETE without WHERE removes all rows \ - ALTER can drop columns, change types, or remove constraints

\ Dump the database before running destructive commands: \ supabase db dump -f backup.sql

\ Check row count first: \ supabase db shell -- -c 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tablename'

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-migration-repair
destructive_patterns.description: supabase migration repair modifies the migration history. This can cause drift between schema and migrations.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase migration repair alters the migration history table:

\ - Can mark migrations as applied or reverted \ - May cause schema drift if used incorrectly \ - Can break future migration runs

\ Review migration status first: \ supabase migration list

\ Dump the database before repairing: \ supabase db dump -f backup.sql

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-migration-down
destructive_patterns.description: supabase migration down reverts applied migrations. Schema changes and associated data may be lost.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase migration down reverts previously applied migrations:

\ - Reversed migrations may DROP tables, columns, or constraints \ - Data in dropped objects is permanently lost \ - With --linked, this targets the remote production database \ - The --version flag can revert multiple migrations at once

\ Review applied migrations first: \ supabase migration list

\ Dump the database before reverting: \ supabase db dump -f backup.sql --linked

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-migration-squash
destructive_patterns.description: supabase migration squash consolidates migrations and omits data manipulation statements (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE).
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase migration squash consolidates multiple migration files into one:

\ - DML statements (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) are omitted \ - Cron jobs, storage buckets, and vault secrets are lost \ - These must be manually recreated in the squashed migration \ - With --linked, modifies the remote migration history

\ Review migrations before squashing: \ supabase migration list

\ Dump the database before squashing: \ supabase db dump -f backup.sql

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-functions-delete
destructive_patterns.description: supabase functions delete removes a deployed Edge Function. This causes immediate downtime for that function.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase functions delete permanently removes a deployed Edge Function:

\ - The function is immediately unavailable \ - Clients calling the function will receive errors \ - The function can be re-deployed from local source code

\ Verify the function first: \ supabase functions list

\ Download source before deleting: \ supabase functions download {function_name}

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-storage-rm
destructive_patterns.description: supabase storage rm deletes objects from storage. With --recursive, entire directories are removed.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase storage rm permanently deletes objects from Supabase Storage:

\ - Deleted files cannot be recovered \ - With --recursive, entire directory trees are removed \ - User-uploaded content may be permanently lost

\ List contents before deleting: \ supabase storage ls {path}

\ Copy files locally before deleting: \ supabase storage cp {path} ./backup/

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-secrets-unset
destructive_patterns.description: supabase secrets unset removes secrets from the project. Edge Functions depending on them will break immediately.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase secrets unset removes environment variables from the project:

\ - Edge Functions depending on these secrets will fail \ - Third-party integrations may break \ - The secret values cannot be retrieved after removal

\ List secrets before removing: \ supabase secrets list

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-projects-delete
destructive_patterns.description: supabase projects delete permanently removes the entire Supabase project and all its data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase projects delete permanently removes a Supabase project:

\ - The database and all data are deleted \ - Auth users and sessions are removed \ - Storage buckets and files are deleted \ - Edge functions are removed \ - API keys are invalidated

\ This action cannot be undone.

\ Dump the database before deleting: \ supabase db dump -f backup.sql --linked

\ Verify the project: \ supabase projects list

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-orgs-delete
destructive_patterns.description: supabase orgs delete permanently removes the organization and may affect all projects within it.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase orgs delete permanently removes a Supabase organization:

\ - All projects in the organization may be affected \ - Billing and subscription are cancelled \ - Team members lose access

\ This action cannot be undone.

\ List organization projects first: \ supabase projects list

\ Verify the organization: \ supabase orgs list

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-branches-delete
destructive_patterns.description: supabase branches delete permanently removes a preview branch and its database.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase branches delete permanently removes a preview database branch:

\ - The branch database and all its data are deleted \ - Any pending migrations on the branch are lost \ - This action cannot be undone

\ Verify the branch first: \ supabase branches list

\ Inspect branch details: \ supabase branches get --id {branch_id}

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-domains-delete
destructive_patterns.description: supabase domains delete removes the custom domain configuration. Clients using the custom domain will lose access.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase domains delete removes the custom hostname configuration:

\ - Clients accessing the service via the custom domain will fail \ - DNS records may need to be reconfigured \ - Re-setup requires DNS verification

\ Check current domain configuration: \ supabase domains get

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-vanity-subdomains-delete
destructive_patterns.description: supabase vanity-subdomains delete removes the vanity subdomain. Clients using it will lose access.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase vanity-subdomains delete removes the vanity subdomain:

\ - Clients using the vanity URL will lose access \ - Auth flows configured with the vanity URL will break \ - The subdomain name may not be reclaimable

\ Check current configuration: \ supabase vanity-subdomains get

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-network-restrictions-update
destructive_patterns.description: supabase network-restrictions update modifies allowed CIDR ranges. Misconfiguration can lock out all database connections.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase network-restrictions update modifies the database firewall rules:

\ - Overly restrictive CIDR ranges can lock out all connections \ - Including your own application servers and admin access \ - Recovery may require Supabase support intervention

\ Check current restrictions first: \ supabase network-restrictions get

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-sso-remove
destructive_patterns.description: supabase sso remove disconnects an SSO identity provider. All users authenticating via that provider will be locked out.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase sso remove disconnects an SSO identity provider:

\ - All users authenticating via that provider are immediately locked out \ - Existing sessions may be invalidated \ - Re-adding the provider requires full reconfiguration

\ List providers before removing: \ supabase sso list

\ Inspect provider details: \ supabase sso show --id {provider_id}

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-config-push
destructive_patterns.description: supabase config push overwrites the remote project configuration with local config.toml settings.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase config push replaces the remote project configuration:

\ - Auth, database, API, and other settings may be overwritten \ - Misconfiguration can break authentication flows \ - Changes take effect immediately on the live project

\ Review your local config.toml before pushing.

destructive_patterns.name: supabase-stop-no-backup
destructive_patterns.description: supabase stop --no-backup stops the local stack and permanently deletes all data volumes.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
supabase stop --no-backup stops the local development stack and deletes data:

\ - All local database data is permanently deleted \ - Storage objects in the local stack are removed \ - Auth users created locally are lost \ - Combined with --all, deletes ALL local Supabase projects' data

\ Use 'supabase stop' without --no-backup to preserve data.
